title: Comfort in Trials - Episode 1: The God of All Comfort

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Good evening, and welcome to Comfort in Trials... <short pause> a brand new series, for the end of your day. <chuckle> My name is David Lee, <short pause> and tonight is episode one: The God of All Comfort.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Over the next few evenings, we'll spend a few quiet minutes together... with words of comfort for hard seasons, rooted in God's promises. <short pause> They're made for the end of your day, so you can slow down... and rest. <short pause> And tonight, we're asking a gentle question... <short pause> where does comfort come from, when trouble comes?

The apostle Paul knew trouble. <short pause> He'd been beaten, shipwrecked, imprisoned, run out of towns. <short pause> And yet he wrote some of the most comforting words in all of Scripture. <short pause> He begins his second letter to the Corinthians... with a blessing, not a complaint.
Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; <long pause>

Paul calls God the Father of mercies... and the God of all comfort. <short pause> Not some comfort. <short pause> All comfort. <short pause> Every bit of true comfort you've ever felt... came from him.
Now Paul tells us why God comforts us.
Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: God comforts you in your trouble... so that you can comfort others in theirs. <short pause> The comfort isn't just for you. <short pause> It's meant to flow through you.

Think about that. <short pause> Your hardest seasons weren't wasted. <short pause> The comfort God gave you then is something you carry now... something you can offer someone else tomorrow. <short pause> Not with advice. Not with solutions. <short pause> With comfort. <short pause> The same tender mercy that held you up.
For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ. <long pause>
This isn't about earning comfort. <short pause> It's about how God meets us. <short pause> When your trouble is deep... his comfort goes deeper still.

Christ himself suffered. <short pause> He was despised, rejected, misunderstood, abandoned. <short pause> He knows what it feels like. <short pause> And because he knows... his comfort is real. <short pause> It's not distant, or theoretical. <short pause> It's the comfort of someone who has been there.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So tonight, if you're carrying something heavy... <exhales> you can bring it to the God of all comfort. <short pause> He isn't surprised by your trouble. <short pause> He isn't put off by it. <short pause> He's the Father of mercies... and he meets you right where you are.

And here's the hope in this. <short pause> The comfort he gives you now... isn't just for now. <short pause> One day, maybe soon, maybe years from now, you'll sit with someone else who's struggling. <short pause> And you'll know what to say... or maybe you'll know not to say anything at all. <short pause> You'll just be present, steady, gentle. <short pause> Because you remember how God was present with you.
That's how comfort works in the kingdom of God. <short pause> It's received... and then it's shared. <short pause> Nothing is wasted.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So as you rest tonight, let yourself receive his comfort. <short pause> You don't have to be strong. <short pause> You don't have to have it all figured out. <short pause> Just bring your weariness, your worry, your heartache. <short pause> He's the God of all comfort... and he's near.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father of mercies, thank you that you comfort us in all our troubles. <short pause> Help us rest in your presence tonight... and when morning comes, help us carry your comfort to someone who needs it. <short pause> Amen.
